title: Fats Atkins, Count Basie's style, and his friendship with Basie
summary: Clarke says Basie got his style from Fats Atkins; he and Basie were close for 35 years and he often sat in with the band.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I know. Right after that -- now this is really strange -- Frank got a job, this job in the Black Cat, with Freddie Greene, you know, after our job ran out on 7th Avenue.
Yeah. Who was the piano player? Can you remember? Because Freddie was talking about him.
Fats Atkins.
Huh?
Fats Atkins. He was the first one that played like Basie.
Really?
Basie got his style -- because Basie played like J.P. Johnson.
Yeah.
But Basie got his style from Fats Atkins.
Now, that's funny Freddie didn't mention that.
Yeah.
Isn't that funny? I guess it just --
Fats Atkins used to (Imitating rhythm.)
Is that right?
That's where Basie got it. Let me show you how it happened.
Because somebody told me -- Jay McShann -- somebody the other day told us, said, that Basie used to sit down and they played two pianos -- I guess --
Uh-huh.
And Basie used to be playing up in the treble. So that's how come he developed that up there.
(Laughter)
The other guy was playing --
But he really --
No, it was Gene Hamey was telling me.
But Basie used to play tunes like,
"Prince Albert," and things like that, it was like J.P. Johnson.
Yeah.

But what happened -- and Basie, we've been tight for about 35 years. I used to just get on his bus and go everywhere. I don't care where -- I'd say, "Where you going, Base?" He'd say, "I'm going to so and so." Okay, I'm going too. I'd just get on the bus and go. Like Freddie and Basie would see that I had something to eat and a place to stay, so I never worried. Sometimes Joe would just say, "Well, I'm not working tonight. Kenny take my place." And I used to play with Basie all the time.
No kidding.
